name: Academy Manufactor
oracle_text: If you would create a Clue, Food, or Treasure token, instead create one of each.
blocked_sentences: If you would create a Clue, Food, or Treasure token, instead create one of each.

needs.what: a static replacement effect that intercepts a token-creation event before the token exists and rewrites what is created -- a filter on the token about to be made (here: subtypes Clue, Food or Treasure) plus a substitute list of token ids to create instead, applied once per creation event and never re-applied to its own output (616.1 / 614.5). The same hook is what Doubling Season, Parallel Lives and Ojer Taq want, so it should take a count multiplier as well as a substitute id list.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `replacements` in the DSL is a four-entry whitelist -- ReplacementModel.event is Literal["self_enters", "self_enters_tapped", "self_enters_with_counters"] -- and every one of them modifies the permanent that is already arriving; none of them can change *what object gets made*. The `create_token` op and `primitives.create_token` take a fixed `def_id` and put the token straight onto the battlefield, firing TOKEN_CREATED only afterwards, so there is no point at which another permanent can see the pending creation and alter it. `replace_deaths` is the only existing effect that redirects an event, and state.py says it acts *after* the death has already happened; it is hardcoded to deaths and has no analogue for creations. The near miss is a `token_created` trigger filtered to subtypes Clue/Food/Treasure with a `create_token` payload for the other two, and it is wrong twice over: the Food and Treasure it creates fire TOKEN_CREATED themselves and match the same filter, so the ability loops without bound and nothing in the trigger vocabulary can tell a token it made from one it did not; and even bounded it would be a trigger, using the stack, so the extra tokens arrive later instead of simultaneously and can be responded to, which changes every "whenever one or more tokens enter" and artifacts-entering count on the board.
needs.note: clue_token, food_token and treasure_token all exist in the token pool, so no token definition is missing -- only the replacement hook.
